the concentration dependences for the quantum efficiency of luminescence emitted from the 4 F3/2 level in neodymium-doped solid-state laser matrices have been measured and that these dependences have been calculated for the first time.

the concentration dependences obtained for the quantum efficiency of luminescence from Nd3+ in different matrices can be used to determine the concentration at which a given matrix becomes a laser medium.

the concentration dependences for the quantum efficiency of luminescence from neodymium-doped laser matrices can be determined from the published data, the authors' own measurements, and calculations based on the proposed model.

the spectroscopic properties and the quantum efficiency of Nd3+ ion luminescence in various matrices.
the spectroscopic properties and the luminescence quantum efficiency of the Nd3+:YAG, Nd3+:YVO4, Nd3+:La2O3, Nd3+:Gd2O3, and Nd3+:CaF2 crystals.
the spectroscopic properties and concentration dependences of quantum efficiencies of the luminescent radiation emitted by neodymiun-activated laser matrices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the concentration dependences for the quantum efficiency of luminescence from 4F3 /2 level in various laser matrices are determined by the multipole interaction between the Nd3+ activator ions.
the concentration dependences for the quantum efficiency of Nd3+ luminescence in laser matrices have been established and that they may be calculated.

the quantum efficiency of luminescence from Nd3+ ions in various solid-state matrices decreases with increase in concentration, and the decrease in quantum efficiency is more marked for the 4F1/2 → 4I11/2 and 4F3 → 4I13/2 transitions than for the 4G7/2 → 2H9/2 transition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quantum efficiency of luminescence of Nd3+ ions in various matrices depends strongly on the concentration of these ions.

the concentration dependences obtained for the quantum efficiency of luminescence from Nd3+ in the 4F32 state in various matrices can be used to determine the optimum concentration of Nd3+ ions in the matrices.
it has shown the possibility of using the method of microscopic determination of the concentration dependences for quantum efficiencies of luminescence from Nd3+ in laser materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quantum efficiency of luminescence from Nd3+ ions in a variety of matrices decreases as the concentration of the activator is increased.
the quantum efficiency of luminescence from Nd3+ in crystals is determined by the concentration of the activator ions and by the nature of the matrix.
the concentration dependence of the quantum efficiency is not a monotonic one.
